name: Metallic Blue
lede: Metallic Blue is a grayish steel blue named by an online color survey, borrowing the vocabulary of car paint for a color that is flat on a screen.

sections.title: A finish, not a pigment
sections.body:
The library records Metallic Blue only from a 2010 crowd-sourced survey, and the nearest ISCC-NBS category is grayish [[blue]], about 5.4 units away [1]. Its nearest named relatives are [[denim]], [[steel-blue]] and [[flat-blue]] [2].

The word *metallic* names a finish and not a hue. Paterson's *Dictionary of Colour* defines it as a lustrous reflective finish, especially in motor vehicles, and uses "metallic blue" as its own example [3]. A lustrous finish is something a flat screen swatch cannot show, so the swatch here is only the average hue [3]. No color book we hold treats metallic blue as a pigment [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Metallic Blue appears in 219 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.92%, as photographed [5]. It peaks in paintings of the 1900s, in 19 of 1,674 (1.1%), 2.4 times the rate expected from the same museums [5]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 42% of the 99 paintings where it counts [5]. The earliest match is from 1301, though the archive is thin in early centuries [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [5].
